findings.title: Storage failure recorded under the legacy duration metric
findings.body: When d.Storage.Create returns an error the code calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...). The metric name (legacy vs storage) is used by dashboards/alerts to distinguish the two backends, so a storage failure ends up inflating the legacy error metric and the storage success metric is never recorded for this path. The success path on line 48 correctly uses recordStorageDuration, so the error branch should mirror it: d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage). The same pattern is repeated in the Update method (line 129).

findings.title: Delete attaches d.Log to context instead of the enriched logger
findings.body: Every other method in this file does `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, log)` using the local `log` variable that already carries name/kind/method. Delete builds that local log on line 96 but then sets `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)`, so the legacy store (and any code reading the logger from the context) only sees the bare DualWriterMode3 logger with mode=3 and loses name, kind, and method. Inconsistent with Create/Get/List/Update/DeleteCollection and reduces observability of async legacy writes.

findings.title: Kind metric label is set to the resource name
findings.body: The success branch of Delete calls d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage). Every other recorder in the file uses options.Kind as the kind label, but here `name` (the resource identifier) is passed instead. This (a) makes the metric inconsistent with the rest of mode 3 and (b) blows up the metric cardinality because each deleted resource name becomes a label value. Should be options.Kind.

findings.title: Storage Update failure recorded under the legacy duration metric
findings.body: Mirrors the bug on line 45. When d.Storage.Update fails, d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) is called, attributing the storage failure to the legacy backend in the metrics. The success branch on line 132 correctly uses recordStorageDuration, so the failure branch should be d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage).

findings.title: Update no longer wraps objInfo for the legacy call
findings.body: The previous implementation precomputed `updated` from the storage copy, then passed an `updateWrapper{upstream: objInfo, updated: ...}` to both Storage.Update and Legacy.Update so both backends received the exact same resolved object. The new code passes the raw objInfo to d.Legacy.Update. If Storage and Legacy disagree on the previous object (e.g. they have drifted) or if objInfo.UpdatedObject behaves differently in the two implementations, the two stores can now persist different versions of the same object, producing data drift between unified storage and legacy storage. This is a real behavioural regression, not just a refactor.

findings.title: Legacy DeleteCollection duration recorded under storage metric
findings.body: In the async goroutine for DeleteCollection the legacy result is timed and then d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy) is called. This is the legacy path, so it should be d.recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy). As written, a legacy DeleteCollection failure silently inflates the storage metric, and the legacy duration histogram never receives any samples from DeleteCollection.

findings.title: Async legacy writes inherit the cancelled request context
findings.body: All four async goroutines (Create line 51, Delete line 110, Update line 135, DeleteCollection line 163) derive their context with context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, 10s, ...). `ctx` is the API server request context, which is cancelled as soon as the handler returns and the response is sent. In practice that means the legacy goroutines often start in an already-cancelled context and the 10-second safety net never has a chance to fire. Result: legacy writes are aborted shortly after the user sees a success response, and because the failure is only logged via metrics, the user has no visibility. For 'safe measure' dual writes this defeats the purpose. Detach from the request lifetime (e.g. context.WithoutCancel or context.Background preserving values) and rely solely on the timeout.

findings.title: TestMode3_Create 'unified store fails' case does not set up the storage mock
findings.body: The second test case sets up only the legacy mock and leaves setupStorageFn nil. Mode3 calls d.Storage.Create before d.Legacy.Create (see dualwriter_mode3.go line 42), so on the testify mock the Storage.Create invocation is unexpected and the test will panic/fail before reaching the legacy mock at all. The test does not exercise the intended path ('storage Create fails, no legacy call'). It needs a setupStorageFn returning an error and either no legacy expectation or an AssertNotCalled for legacy.

findings.title: No test verifies that the async legacy write actually happens
findings.body: TestMode3_Create, TestMode3_Update, TestMode3_Delete and TestMode3_DeleteCollection all set up the legacy mock with m.On(...) but never assert that it was called (no mock.AssertCalled for the legacy backend). The goroutine in dualwriter_mode3.go has no synchronization with the test, so on a fast machine the test function can return and t.Run can finish before the goroutine has dispatched, meaning a regression that simply removed the goroutine would still pass the tests. Add an explicit AssertCalled (and ideally a small synchronization point) to prove the async write really happened.

findings.title: TestMode3_Get creates a local Prometheus registry instead of using the package-level `p`
findings.body: All other tests in this file (and the matching Mode1 tests in dualwriter_mode1_test.go, which were just refactored away from this pattern in the same PR) use the shared `var p = prometheus.NewRegistry()` declared in dualwriter_mode1_test.go. TestMode3_Get introduces a local `p := prometheus.NewRegistry()` on line 119. It works but is inconsistent and looks like a missed cleanup. Use the shared registry.
